name: Chai-1 (Chai Discovery)
origin_detail: Chai Discovery, a venture-backed startup; the launch post names OpenAI, Thrive Capital, Dimension, Conviction, Neo, Lachy Groom and Amplify Partners among its backers.

licences.data: training data not stated on fetched pages

openness_notes: v0.0.1 ('Initial release of Chai-1', 09 Sep [2024]) shipped under the 'Chai Discovery Community License Agreement'. It granted rights 'SOLELY FOR NON-COMMERCIAL PURPOSES' to the 'Chai-1 Model software code and model weights', gave commercial entities no rights, barred offering it as a service, and had an acceptable-use policy restricting use of outputs to train other protein models. The web interface was free 'including for commercial applications such as drug discovery'. v0.4.0 (27 Nov [2024]), titled 'Apache 2.0 license (commercial use)', changed code and weights to Apache-2.0. The successor Chai-2 is only cited in the chai-lab repo, and the homepage presents it through pharma partnerships (Novartis, Pfizer, Eli Lilly, argenx) with no open release found. Initial 1; current 2 (open older model, unreleased flagship).

risk_events: Successor model (Chai-2) offered through partnerships rather than released
robustness: Apache-2.0 Chai-1 code and weights can be forked; future models are at the company's discretion.
physical_science_relevance: Protein, ligand and nucleic-acid complex prediction for drug discovery.

training_data.note: Not described in the README; templates are downloaded from RCSB at inference time.

openness_effect_assessment: Chai-1 started with a non-commercial licence and switched to Apache-2.0 within three months, as MIT-licensed rivals appeared. The company then kept its next-generation antibody model for partnerships, and per its homepage it raised a $400M Series C.
key_takeaway: A startup used an open (eventually Apache-2.0) model as a calling card while keeping its frontier model closed, a typical AI-startup open-core pattern.
